change_interpretations.engineering_summary: The brake‑override requirement now adds a timing constraint: the emergency brake command must be issued within 80 ms of the brake input, tightening the previous unlimited response.

assessments.reason: The test validates accelerator‑torque response (VCU-DR-01) and does not involve brake‑override timing.
The test exercises brake‑pedal arbitration but does not record the brake‑command latency required by the new 80 ms limit.
evidence: Procedure applies emergency brake with 85 % pedal
assessments.recommended_action: Add measurement of brake command latency and verify it meets ≤80 ms.

assessments.reason: The test checks high‑load torque transients and has no reference to brake‑override behavior.
evidence: Procedure sweeps torque demand; no brake requirement linked

assessments.reason: The test measures emergency‑brake command latency against a 100 ms threshold; the new 80 ms limit makes the previous PASS (88 ms) invalid.
assessments.recommended_action: Update the test threshold to 80 ms and re‑run using the same clock as specified.

assessments.reason: The test validates wheel‑speed sensor failure handling, unrelated to the brake‑override timing change.
The test audits mode‑change logging, which does not involve brake‑override timing.
The test has a TBD requirement link and focuses on acceleration under thermal load, not brake‑override timing.
evidence: Procedure uses 80 % pedal; no brake reference

assessments.reason: The test references an unknown legacy requirement and does not address brake‑override timing.
The test compares torque ramps between driving modes; brake‑override timing is not exercised.
The test validates pedal‑signal spike filtering per VCU-DR-02, unrelated to brake‑override timing.
The test checks torque cancellation during emergency braking but does not measure the 80 ms command issuance deadline introduced by the change.
evidence: Procedure verifies positive torque drop on emergency brake
assessments.recommended_action: Extend the test to capture brake command latency and verify it is ≤80 ms.

assessments.reason: The wake‑up timing test concerns ECU power‑up readiness and does not involve brake‑override behavior.
